title: Eruin, a rpg with unscripted dialogue
author: Ok-Dimension-741
selftext:
Hi guys, for quite some time now, I have been working on a stupid idea of mine, It took me a long time to reach this point but I am finally close to a demo. 

Llms finally enabled such mechanics and I am very excited to hear what people think about it. I think the demo will be put in a few weeks so please check it put and let me know what you think.

Www..eruin.dev

comments.author: cxfoulke
comments.body:
llms are absolutely terrible for fiction and have pretty big context rot in longer chats?  seems like a hard issue to get around. 

Might be interesting to have an llm as a text parser that picks the most relevant human dialog to play.   
Even just in your trailer it feels like llm speak. 

If the best models in the world are bad at fiction writing... how bad are the llms you can build into a game gonna be? 

Also rpgs defenitly need text skip, id make sure you have some way of handling that.

replies.author: Ok-Dimension-741
replies.body:
Fair points, thanks for actually watching the trailer. To clarify the design: the LLM isn't writing the story. Quests, lore and structure are handwritten; the model plays characters inside that frame. Each NPC gets a fixed persona plus only the relevant lore and recent history, so there's no long chat to rot. Things like riddle judging use constrained structured output, not free text.
The "LLM speak" criticism is valid though, and it's the thing I'm working hardest on right now (fine-tuning the NPC models on character voice). And yes, you can interrupt, walk away mid-sentence, or skip lines.
